beats.intent: 2³ drawn as three tiles of 2 multiplied together
beats.narration: Two cubed means three twos multiplied together.
beats.code:
stage.title("Multiplying powers")
row3 = VGroup(*[VGroup(Square(0.8, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5), Text("2", font_size=34)) for _ in range(3)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.35).move_to([-3.6, 1.4, 0])
stage.play(FadeIn(row3))
stage.add(row3)
stage.play(*[FadeIn(Text("×", font_size=30).move_to((row3[i].get_right() + row3[i + 1].get_left()) / 2)) for i in range(2)])
stage.label(row3, "2³", direction=LEFT, color=BLUE)

row2 = VGroup(*[VGroup(Square(0.8, color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.5), Text("2", font_size=34)) for _ in range(2)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.35).next_to(row3, DOWN, buff=0.6, aligned_edge=LEFT)
stage.play(FadeIn(row2))
stage.add(row2)
stage.play(FadeIn(Text("×", font_size=30).move_to((row2[0].get_right() + row2[1].get_left()) / 2)))
stage.label(row2, "2²", direction=LEFT, color=ORANGE)

beats.intent: All five tiles in one row: five twos multiplied, 32
beats.narration: Multiply them together and you just have five twos in a row: two to the fifth, thirty two.
beats.code:
row5 = VGroup(*[VGroup(Square(0.8, color=BLUE if i < 3 else ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.5), Text("2", font_size=34)) for i in range(5)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.35).move_to([-2.8, -1.6, 0])
stage.play(TransformFromCopy(VGroup(row3, row2), row5))
stage.add(row5)
stage.play(*[FadeIn(Text("×", font_size=30).move_to((row5[i].get_right() + row5[i + 1].get_left()) / 2)) for i in range(4)])
stage.label(row5, "2⁵ = 32", direction=DOWN, color=GREEN)

beats.narration: Multiplying powers of the same number adds the counts: three plus two is five.

request: a rod is 4.5 cm to the nearest millimetre: how long could it really be?

beats.intent: A number line from 4.3 to 4.7 with 4.5 marked as the measurement
beats.narration: A rod measures four point five centimetres, to the nearest millimetre.
beats.code:
stage.title("Upper and lower bounds")
nl = NumberLine(x_range=[4.3, 4.7, 0.05], length=10, include_numbers=False).move_to([0, -0.5, 0])
nums = VGroup(*[Text(f"{v:.1f}", font_size=26).next_to(nl.n2p(v), DOWN, buff=0.25) for v in (4.3, 4.4, 4.5, 4.6, 4.7)])
stage.play(Create(nl), FadeIn(nums))
stage.add(nl, nums)
m = Dot(nl.n2p(4.5), color=YELLOW, radius=0.1)
stage.play(FadeIn(m))
stage.add(m)
stage.label(m, "measured: 4.5", direction=UP, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: Lengths that round to 4.5 shaded green from 4.45 to 4.55; 4.44 and 4.56 in red outside
beats.narration: Anything from four point four five up to just under four point five five rounds to four point five. Four point four four rounds down to four point four; four point five six rounds up to four point six.
beats.code:
band = Rectangle(width=nl.n2p(4.55)[0] - nl.n2p(4.45)[0], height=0.5, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=0).move_to((nl.n2p(4.45) + nl.n2p(4.55)) / 2)
stage.play(FadeIn(band))
stage.add(band)
outs = VGroup(*[Dot(nl.n2p(v), color=RED, radius=0.08) for v in (4.44, 4.56)])
stage.play(FadeIn(outs))
stage.add(outs)
stage.label(outs[0], "4.44 → 4.4", direction=UP + LEFT, color=RED)
stage.label(outs[1], "4.56 → 4.6", direction=UP + RIGHT, color=RED)

beats.intent: A filled dot at 4.45 (lower bound) and an open circle at 4.55 (upper bound)
beats.narration: The lower bound, four point four five, is included. The upper bound, four point five five, is not: it would round up.
beats.code:
lo = Dot(nl.n2p(4.45), color=GREEN, radius=0.1)
hi = Circle(radius=0.1, color=GREEN, stroke_width=4).move_to(nl.n2p(4.55))
stage.play(FadeIn(lo), Create(hi))
stage.add(lo, hi)
stage.play(FadeIn(Text("lower: 4.45", font_size=26, color=GREEN).move_to(nl.n2p(4.45) + 1.3 * DOWN + 0.6 * LEFT)), FadeIn(Text("upper: 4.55", font_size=26, color=GREEN).move_to(nl.n2p(4.55) + 1.3 * DOWN + 0.6 * RIGHT)))

beats.narration: So the true length is at least four point four five and less than four point five five.

request: why are angles in the same segment of a circle equal?

beats.intent: A circle with a chord AB across its lower part
beats.narration: Draw a circle and a chord A B.
beats.code:
stage.title("Angles in the same segment")
c = np.array([-3, -0.3, 0])
R = 2.2
P = lambda deg: c + R * np.array([np.cos(deg * DEGREES), np.sin(deg * DEGREES), 0])
circle = Circle(radius=R, color=WHITE).move_to(c)
A, B = P(210), P(330)
chord = Line(A, B, color=BLUE)
stage.play(Create(circle), Create(chord))
stage.add(circle, chord)
stage.play(FadeIn(Text("A", font_size=28).move_to(c + 1.15 * (A - c))), FadeIn(Text("B", font_size=28).move_to(c + 1.15 * (B - c))))

beats.intent: A point C on the upper arc joined to A and B, the angle at C marked 60°
beats.narration: Pick any point C on the big arc and join it to A and B. The angle at C is sixty degrees.
beats.code:
C = P(100)
tri_c = VGroup(Line(C, A), Line(C, B)).set_color(YELLOW)
ang_c = Angle(Line(C, A), Line(C, B), radius=0.5, color=YELLOW)
stage.play(Create(tri_c), Create(ang_c))
stage.add(tri_c, ang_c)
stage.play(FadeIn(Text("C", font_size=28).move_to(c + 1.12 * (C - c))))
stage.label(ang_c, "60°", direction=DOWN, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: A second point D on the same arc, its angle to A and B also 60°
beats.narration: Pick another point D on the same arc. Its angle is sixty degrees too.
beats.code:
D = P(40)
tri_d = VGroup(Line(D, A), Line(D, B)).set_color(GREEN)
ang_d = Angle(Line(D, A), Line(D, B), radius=0.5, color=GREEN)
stage.play(Create(tri_d), Create(ang_d))
stage.add(tri_d, ang_d)
stage.play(FadeIn(Text("D", font_size=28).move_to(c + 1.12 * (D - c))))
stage.label(ang_d, "60°", direction=LEFT, color=GREEN)

beats.intent: Radii OA and OB with the 120° angle at the centre, beside ∠ACB = ∠ADB = ½ × 120° = 60°
beats.narration: Both are half the angle at the centre, a hundred and twenty degrees, so they must be equal.
beats.code:
radii = VGroup(Line(c, A), Line(c, B)).set_color(ORANGE)
ang_o = Angle(Line(c, A), Line(c, B), radius=0.4, color=ORANGE)
stage.play(Create(radii), Create(ang_o))
stage.add(radii, ang_o)
stage.label(ang_o, "120°", direction=DOWN, color=ORANGE)
stage.equation(r"\angle ACB = \angle ADB", r"= \tfrac{1}{2} \times 120^\circ = 60^\circ")

request: how do you find the nth term of 3, 7, 11, 15, ...?

beats.intent: The first four terms drawn as stacks of 3, 7, 11 and 15 dots
beats.narration: Here's a sequence drawn as stacks of dots: three, seven, eleven, fifteen.
beats.code:
stage.title("The nth term")
xs = [-5.0, -3.6, -2.2, -0.8]
stacks = VGroup(*[VGroup(*[Dot([x, -2.5 + 0.28 * j, 0], radius=0.1, color=BLUE) for j in range(4 * (n + 1) - 1)]) for n, x in enumerate(xs)])
stage.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(s) for s in stacks], lag_ratio=0.3))
stage.add(stacks)
stage.play(*[FadeIn(Text(f"n = {n + 1}", font_size=22).move_to([x, -3.0, 0])) for n, x in enumerate(xs)])

beats.intent: +4 marked between each pair of stacks
beats.narration: Each stack has four more dots than the one before.
beats.code:
hops = VGroup(*[CurvedArrow([xs[i] + 0.2, -2.5 + 0.28 * (4 * (i + 1) - 1) + 0.2, 0], [xs[i + 1] - 0.2, -2.5 + 0.28 * (4 * (i + 2) - 1) + 0.2, 0], angle=-PI / 3, color=YELLOW) for i in range(3)])
stage.play(Create(hops))
stage.add(hops)
stage.play(*[FadeIn(Text("+4", font_size=24, color=YELLOW).next_to(h, UP, buff=0.05)) for h in hops])

beats.intent: A hollow dot on top of each stack showing 4n, one more than the term
beats.narration: Going up in fours means it's linked to the four times table: four, eight, twelve, sixteen. Each stack is one short of that.
beats.code:
ghosts = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.1, color=ORANGE).move_to([x, -2.5 + 0.28 * (4 * (n + 1) - 1), 0]) for n, x in enumerate(xs)])
stage.play(FadeIn(ghosts))
stage.add(ghosts)
stage.label(ghosts, "4n, minus 1", direction=RIGHT, color=ORANGE)

beats.intent: The stacks beside nth term = 4n − 1, and the 100th term = 399
beats.narration: So the nth term is four n minus one. The hundredth term is four hundred minus one, three hundred and ninety nine.
